overview: Megasphaera is a genus of strictly anaerobic, Gram-negative cocci (family Veillonellaceae) that ferment lactate and sugars into short-chain fatty acids. It is enriched in the sputum and airway of active-tuberculosis patients,<sup>[1]</sup> where its short-chain fatty acid output is thought to push local immunity toward tolerogenic, anti-inflammatory responses that can blunt protective anti-Mtb defence.<sup>[2]</sup> It is otherwise a normal commensal of the gut and mouth.
nutritional immunity: As an obligate anaerobe, Megasphaera centres its energy metabolism on iron-sulfur chemistry, using [4Fe-4S] ferredoxin and flavin-based electron bifurcation (the butyryl-CoA dehydrogenase and EtfAB complex), so its iron demand is high and is met from the soluble ferrous iron of anoxic niches.<sup>[3]</sup> It can swap an FMN flavodoxin in for ferredoxin, a recognised iron-sparing tactic under iron limitation.<sup>[3]</sup> Genus-specific siderophores and metal-efflux systems are not characterised.
metallomic signature: Its enrichment fits the iron environment of active TB: as serum iron falls but macrophages and necrotic, hemorrhagic cavities load with iron, anaerobic fermenters that draw on abundant ferrous iron are favoured.<sup>[1]</sup> No direct per-organism measurements link Megasphaera to the patient copper or zinc findings, so this is an ecological inference rather than a measured metal tie.
oxygen ecology: Megasphaera is a strict anaerobe, and its enrichment marks the diseased lung's shift toward an oxygen-poor community. Cavitary necrosis and mucus plugging create the hypoxic, reducing microenvironments such fermenters need,<sup>[1]</sup> while its electron-bifurcating enzymes generate damaging superoxide on exposure to air, an Achilles heel that confines it to anoxic niches.<sup>[3]</sup>

1. Kayongo A, et al. Airway microbiome signature discriminates M. tuberculosis infection status. iScience. 2024. link
  2. Lachmandas E, et al. Diabetes, short-chain fatty acids and increased tuberculosis susceptibility. J Diabetes Res. 2016. link
  3. Chowdhury NP, Kahnt J, Buckel W. Reduction of ferredoxin or oxygen by flavin-based electron bifurcation in Megasphaera elsdenii. FEBS J. 2015. link

overview: Mycobacterium is a genus of aerobic, acid-fast actinobacteria with a mycolic-acid-rich, lipid-dense envelope; it includes Mycobacterium tuberculosis, the cause of TB. It is the defining enriched taxon of the active-disease airway signature,<sup>[1]</sup> reflecting replication inside alveolar macrophages and granulomas rather than commensal carriage.
nutritional immunity: Mtb is an intracellular iron pirate: it scavenges host iron from transferrin, lactoferrin, ferritin and heme using the siderophores mycobactin and carboxymycobactin, taken up through the IrtAB transporter, all essential for survival inside macrophages.<sup>[2]</sup> The regulator IdeR derepresses these systems under the iron starvation the host imposes through hepcidin, lactoferrin and siderocalin, and IdeR is itself required for virulence.<sup>[3]</sup>
metallomic signature: Mtb does not merely sit in the patient metallome, it drives it: the host lowers serum iron and floods the phagosome with copper and zinc while withholding iron and manganese, the battle that defines the TB metal signature.<sup>[2]</sup> Mtb counters copper and zinc intoxication with dedicated efflux systems, so its enrichment reflects an organism built to survive the host's metal warfare.<sup>[2]</sup>
oxygen ecology: Mtb is an obligate aerobe, so its growth tracks oxygen: it favours the well-aerated upper lung and is enriched in oxygen-rich cavitary disease,<sup>[1]</sup> while granuloma hypoxia forces it into a non-replicating, drug-tolerant state. This is why oxygenation strategies that relieve hypoxia risk reactivating it rather than restraining it.
references:
1. Kayongo A, et al. Airway microbiome signature discriminates M. tuberculosis infection status. iScience. 2024. link
  2. Neyrolles O, et al. Mycobacteria, metals, and the macrophage. Immunol Rev. 2015. link
  3. Pandey R, Rodriguez GM. IdeR is required for iron homeostasis and virulence in Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Mol Microbiol. 2013. link

overview: Prevotella is a genus of Gram-negative, obligately anaerobic Bacteroidota that dominate the mouth and upper airway. It is repeatedly enriched in TB sputum as part of a progression-associated dysbiotic signature,<sup>[1]</sup> and the influx of such oral anaerobes into the lung drives a Th17 inflammatory tone.<sup>[3]</sup>
nutritional immunity: Like other host-associated Bacteroidota, Prevotella is heme- and iron-dependent and cannot make protoporphyrin de novo, so it must scavenge heme and iron from the host. Prevotella intermedia binds hemoglobin through a roughly 60 kDa outer-membrane protein (strongest at acidic pH) and liberates heme via a cysteine protease,<sup>[2]</sup> feeding iron uptake through TonB-dependent receptors and Feo systems under Fur control. This heme appetite sets it against host iron and heme sequestration.
metallomic signature: Its enrichment fits the patient metallome of cavitary TB: hypoxic, hemorrhagic, heme- and iron-rich lesions are exactly the niche a heme-scavenging anaerobe exploits, even as the host lowers serum iron.<sup>[2]</sup> Zinc, manganese and copper handling are not defined at the genus level, so the metallomic tie rests on its documented heme and iron dependence.
oxygen ecology: Prevotella is an obligate anaerobe, and its airway enrichment is a hallmark of the diseased lung's shift to an anoxic, oral-type community.<sup>[1]</sup> Microaspiration seeds these oral anaerobes into hypoxic, mucus-plugged and necrotic lower-airway niches, where the oral-taxa pneumotype sustains a Th17 inflammatory phenotype.<sup>[3]</sup>

overview: Alistipes is a genus of Gram-negative, bile-tolerant, strictly anaerobic rods (family Rikenellaceae, phylum Bacteroidota) of the distal gut that ferment amino acids and contribute to short-chain fatty acid production (notably propionate and succinate).<sup>[1]</sup> It matters in TB via the gut-lung axis: it is enriched, with 16S studies finding Alistipes (with Bacteroides and Blautia) raised in latent TB infection among patients with poorly controlled diabetes, as part of a six-taxon gut signature that tracks lower serum IL-17F and TNF-alpha.<sup>[2]</sup>
nutritional immunity: Like other Bacteroidota, Alistipes is not expected to make siderophores; the phylum is established as non-siderophore-producing and instead uses TonB-dependent transporters to scavenge heme and host or dietary iron, with Bacteroides preferring heme over soluble ferrous iron.<sup>[1]</sup> Under iron starvation Bacteroides also pirate exogenous ferri-siderophores from neighbours via the XusABC system, a strategy plausibly shared by bile-tolerant gut anaerobes.<sup>[1]</sup> This heme and iron foraging lets such anaerobes thrive in the metal-competitive gut, fitting its enriched status.
oxygen ecology: Alistipes is a strict anaerobe, growing only in the anoxic distal gut where it ferments amino acids to short-chain fatty acids.<sup>[1]</sup> Its enrichment in the TB signature is a gut-compartment finding rather than airway colonisation, so it does not occupy the hypoxic granuloma directly; instead its expansion reflects gut-lung-axis dysbiosis in latent TB with poorly controlled diabetes, where the enriched anaerobe correlates with dampened systemic immunity.<sup>[2]</sup>
references:
1. Silale A, et al. Structural basis of iron piracy by human gut Bacteroides. Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A. 2026. link
  2. Huang HL, et al. Gut microbiota composition can reflect immune responses of latent tuberculosis infection in patients with poorly controlled diabetes. Respir Res. 2023. link

overview: Campylobacter is a genus of microaerophilic, Gram-negative spiral Epsilonproteobacteria, best known as enteric pathogens but also found as oral and airway commensals. It is enriched in the TB signature, clustering with Mycobacterium tuberculosis in sputum-microbiome analyses, consistent with a shift toward microaerophilic taxa in the diseased lung.<sup>[1]</sup>
nutritional immunity: Campylobacter is heavily iron-dependent, with metal acquisition governed by the Fur regulator. It makes no siderophore of its own but pirates exogenous chelates and host iron through multiple TonB-dependent receptors (ferric-enterobactin, heme, transferrin and lactoferrin iron).<sup>[2]</sup> Zinc is scavenged under host restriction by the Zur-regulated ZnuABC importer, and copper is detoxified by CopA efflux, all set against host calprotectin and lactoferrin.<sup>[2]</sup>
oxygen ecology: Campylobacter is microaerophilic, requiring low oxygen tensions, so it is favoured by the intermediate-oxygen, mucus-laden zones of the TB-disrupted airway rather than fully oxic or fully anoxic niches.<sup>[1]</sup> Its reliance on an iron-cofactored superoxide dismutase, rather than a manganese one, ties its oxidative-stress tolerance directly to iron availability.<sup>[2]</sup>
references:
1. Kayongo A, et al. Airway microbiome signature discriminates M. tuberculosis infection status. iScience. 2024. link
  2. Stahl M, Butcher J, Stintzi A. Nutrient acquisition and metabolism by Campylobacter jejuni. Front Cell Infect Microbiol. 2012. link

overview: Eubacterium is a genus of obligately anaerobic, Gram-positive Clostridia and a core colonic commensal that ferments dietary fibre into butyrate and other short-chain fatty acids. In the gut it is reported enriched in active TB,<sup>[1]</sup> where excess butyrate may be counterproductive, dampening the IFN-gamma and Th17 responses needed against Mtb.<sup>[2]</sup>
nutritional immunity: As a strict anaerobe, Eubacterium relies on iron-sulfur and ferredoxin or flavodoxin enzymes, so iron is its dominant metal need, taken as soluble ferrous iron through Feo-type transporters rather than siderophores, under Fur control (extrapolated from the gut Clostridia model Clostridioides difficile).<sup>[3]</sup> Its relevance to TB is via the gut-lung axis and systemic iron sequestration, not the airway phagosome.<sup>[1]</sup>
oxygen ecology: Eubacterium is an obligate anaerobe confined to the anoxic colon, so its TB association is a gut-compartment, gut-lung-axis finding rather than airway colonisation.<sup>[1]</sup> Its enrichment shifts luminal fermentation toward butyrate, an immunometabolic rather than oxygen-niche effect on TB immunity.<sup>[2]</sup>
references:
1. Alvarado-Pena N, et al. The microbiome and the gut-lung axis in tuberculosis. Front Microbiol. 2023. link
  2. Lachmandas E, et al. Diabetes, short-chain fatty acids and increased tuberculosis susceptibility. J Diabetes Res. 2016. link
  3. Berges M, et al. Iron regulation in Clostridioides difficile. Front Microbiol. 2018. link

overview: Kingella is a genus of fastidious, capnophilic Gram-negative coccobacilli (family Neisseriaceae) that live as commensals of the oropharynx. It appears within the disrupted oral and airway flora of TB and has been reported enriched in TB sputum, including in multidrug-resistant disease, as part of the expansion of oral-origin Proteobacteria in the inflamed lung.<sup>[1]</sup>
nutritional immunity: Genus-specific metal data for Kingella are sparse; by the Neisseriaceae model, iron and zinc are acquired through TonB-dependent receptors rather than siderophores, including transferrin- and lactoferrin-binding proteins and zinc-piracy transporters that strip Zn and Mn from host calprotectin, under Fur and Zur control.<sup>[2]</sup> Direct confirmation in Kingella itself is lacking.
oxygen ecology: Kingella is capnophilic, growing best in carbon-dioxide-enriched, reduced-oxygen conditions, fitting the intermediate-oxygen mucosal niches of the oral-origin community that expands in the diseased airway.<sup>[1]</sup>
references:
1. Kayongo A, et al. Airway microbiome signature discriminates M. tuberculosis infection status. iScience. 2024. link
  2. Branch AH, et al. Acclimation to nutritional immunity and metal intoxication in the pathogenic Neisseriaceae. Front Cell Infect Microbiol. 2022. link

overview: Streptococcus is a genus of facultatively anaerobic, catalase-negative Gram-positive cocci that dominate the mouth and upper airway. It is among the most abundant genera in TB sputum and is enriched in the signature, though its relative abundance is variable and tends to be higher in less severe disease.<sup>[1]</sup>
nutritional immunity: Streptococci run a manganese-centric metallome: being catalase-negative, they depend on imported Mn(II) (via PsaA-type ABC importers) to power manganese superoxide dismutase and survive oxidative stress.<sup>[2]</sup> Iron is taken up largely through heme and Fe/Mn ABC transporters rather than siderophores, with zinc handled by AdcR-controlled importers and a CzcD efflux pump; host calprotectin chelates Mn and Zn to starve them of both.<sup>[2]</sup>
metallomic signature: Its metal economy meets the TB patient metallome at zinc and manganese: as the host deploys calprotectin to withhold Mn and Zn and serum zinc falls, excess zinc can displace manganese from the streptococcal PsaA uptake site and cripple manganese-dependent oxidative defence.<sup>[2]</sup> Its variable enrichment is thus sensitive to the same Mn and Zn restriction that shapes the inflamed airway.
oxygen ecology: Streptococcus is aerotolerant and facultatively anaerobic, which lets it persist across the airway oxygen gradient as the community shifts toward anaerobes.<sup>[1]</sup> Lacking catalase, it leans on manganese-based rather than heme-based defences against the oxidative stress of the inflamed lung.<sup>[2]</sup>
references:
1. Kayongo A, et al. Airway microbiome signature discriminates M. tuberculosis infection status. iScience. 2024. link
  2. Akbari MS, Doran KS, Burcham LR. Metal homeostasis in pathogenic streptococci. Microorganisms. 2022. link

overview: Arachnia (Pseudopropionibacterium propionicum) is a Gram-positive, aerotolerant anaerobic, filamentous member of the Propionibacteriaceae and a normal commensal of the mouth and upper airway. It is depleted in the TB airway, consistent with the broad loss of oral commensal actinobacteria that marks TB-associated dysbiosis.<sup>[1]</sup>
oxygen ecology: Arachnia is an aerotolerant anaerobe of oxygen-stable oral surfaces; its depletion is part of the collapse of commensal diversity as the TB lung shifts toward a disease-associated community.<sup>[1]</sup>
references: 1. Kayongo A, et al. Airway microbiome signature discriminates M. tuberculosis infection status. iScience. 2024. link

overview: Cardiobacterium is a fastidious, capnophilic Gram-negative genus (family Cardiobacteriaceae; the C of the HACEK group) that lives as a commensal of the mouth and upper airway and rarely causes endocarditis.<sup>[2]</sup> It is depleted in the TB signature, in line with the loss of oral and upper-airway commensals in TB dysbiosis.<sup>[1]</sup>
oxygen ecology: Cardiobacterium is capnophilic, favouring carbon-dioxide-enriched, reduced-oxygen mucosal niches; its depletion reflects disruption of the stable oral and upper-airway community in TB rather than any direct role in disease.<sup>[1]</sup>
references:
1. Kayongo A, et al. Airway microbiome signature discriminates M. tuberculosis infection status. iScience. 2024. link
  2. Fisher J, Garrett EM. The Brief Case: Cardiobacterium hominis endocarditis in a pediatric patient. J Clin Microbiol. 2024. link

overview: Solobacterium (S. moorei) is a Gram-positive, obligately anaerobic bacillus (Erysipelotrichaceae) of the mouth and gut, linked to halitosis and periodontal disease. It is scored as depleted here, though its reported direction in TB is inconsistent (some sputum analyses find it co-occurring with Mycobacterium tuberculosis), so its placement should be read cautiously.<sup>[1]</sup>
oxygen ecology: Solobacterium is an obligate anaerobe of the tongue and gut; in the airway it appears as an oral-derived anaerobe, but its inconsistent direction across TB studies makes its oxygen-niche interpretation tentative.<sup>[1]</sup>
references: 1. Kayongo A, et al. Airway microbiome signature discriminates M. tuberculosis infection status. iScience. 2024. link

overview: Prevotella melaninogenica is a Gram-negative, black-pigmented obligate anaerobe (phylum Bacteroidota) and a core oral and upper-airway commensal. It is among the taxa enriched in TB sputum, consistent with the oral-to-airway dysbiosis and microaspiration of pulmonary TB.<sup>[1]</sup> Its lower-airway abundance varies across cohorts, so it reads as a marker of an oral-flora shift rather than a TB pathogen.
nutritional immunity: Like other Bacteroidota, P. melaninogenica is heme-auxotrophic: it cannot make protoporphyrin IX de novo and must scavenge hemin from host hemoproteins, accumulating a surface iron(III)-protoporphyrin pigment from hemoglobin. By the Bacteroides model, iron is freed from heme in the periplasm and assimilated through the FeoAB ferrous-iron transporter with CobN-like BtuS proteins.<sup>[2]</sup> This heme dependence sets it against host haptoglobin, hemopexin and hepcidin-driven iron sequestration.
metallomic signature: Its enrichment fits the patient metallome of cavitary TB: hemorrhagic, iron- and heme-rich necrotic lesions are the niche a heme-scavenging anaerobe exploits, even as serum iron falls.<sup>[2]</sup> The accumulated ferri-heme surface pigment also carries catalase-like activity that detoxifies peroxide. Zinc, manganese and copper handling are not defined for the species.
oxygen ecology: P. melaninogenica is an obligate anaerobe; its airway enrichment marks the diseased lung's shift to an anoxic, oral-type community seeded by microaspiration into hypoxic, mucus-plugged niches,<sup>[1]</sup> where the oral-taxa pneumotype sustains a Th17 inflammatory tone.<sup>[3]</sup>

overview: Segatella oris (formerly Prevotella oris) is a Gram-negative, obligately anaerobic, saccharolytic member of the Bacteroidota/Prevotellaceae that normally resides in the oral cavity. In TB it is one of the oral-origin anaerobes enriched in the diseased lower airway and sputum, reflecting the shift toward an anaerobic, oral-type community,<sup>[1]</sup> and is a marker of dysbiosis rather than a primary pathogen.
nutritional immunity: Like other host-associated Bacteroidota, Segatella and Prevotella lack de novo heme synthesis and require hemin as a growth factor, scavenging iron-protoporphyrin from the host; P. oris secretes a thiol-activated hemolysin that liberates hemoglobin-bound heme. By the Bacteroides model, iron freed from heme is assimilated through FeoAB with CobN-like BtuS proteins.<sup>[2]</sup> This heme appetite places it against host iron and heme sequestration.
metallomic signature: Its enrichment suits the heme- and iron-rich, hypoxic cavitary niche of active TB, where heme-scavenging anaerobes are favoured as the host lowers serum iron.<sup>[2]</sup> Species-level zinc, manganese and copper handling are uncharacterised, so the tie rests on its documented heme and iron dependence.
oxygen ecology: Segatella oris is an obligate anaerobe; its presence in sputum reflects microaspiration of oral anaerobes into the oxygen-depleted, mucus-laden lower airway that develops in TB.<sup>[1]</sup>
